name: robust-latex-formula-extraction
conclusion: robust-latex-formula-extraction (Ask) specifies 3 of 5 categories: 3 autonomy limits, 3 clarification rules, 6 validation rules; none for approval gates, escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 3 autonomy limits (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list: shell here-docs for writing LaTeX; background converters without logs or timeouts.

statements.quote: Write the file using a language-native file writer (e.g., Python), not shell here-docs, to avoid quoting/escaping corruption.
Avoid running converters in the background without streaming logs. Use explicit timeouts and check for actual output files before proceeding.
Use a safe writer (Python/Open file APIs). Don’t pipe complex TeX through shell here-docs with nested quotes.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 3 clarification rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list: inventing missing or unreadable formula parts; guessing uncertain syntax fixes.

statements.quote: Do not infer or invent missing parts. If the text extraction drops special symbols and you cannot recover them reliably, mark the formula as problematic and avoid hallucinating replacements.
If unsure about a fix, do not guess. Leave the original and flag the issue in your notes (not in the output file unless the task demands).
Only transcribe what you can extract from text/layout. If a piece is unreadable, don’t invent it.

validation.conclusion: 6 validation rules (6 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: 1-page smoke test before scaling up; timeouts and output artifact checks; structural and content checks before delivery.

statements.quote: Run a 1-page smoke test with a short timeout and capture logs. Confirm expected output (e.g., presence of math blocks) before scaling up.
Never leave long-running processes unattended. Always set timeouts and check for actual output artifacts before continuing.
